summary: Redwood AE + SE walked AtlasBio through the Console's per-route cost forensics, usage analytics, and anomaly detection. Customer is evaluating hosted vs Dedicated; FinOps wants chargeback-ready reports and exportable datasets. Security questions raised around KMS, SSO, and audit logs.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-18 15:00 UTC | Duration 46m
Attendees: Sophie Raines (Redwood AE), Daniel Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (AtlasBio - Head of ML), Carlos Vega (AtlasBio - Platform), Priya Patel (AtlasBio - FinOps), Tom Hsu (AtlasBio - CTO)

Summary: Quick console deep dive focused on per-route chargeback, how to split costs by team/model, and how anomalies are surfaced. Demo included live filtering, route tags, and a sample export.

00:00:12 Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. We'll do a roughly 35 minute tour and leave time for questions. Daniel will drive the console and I'll jump in for pricing and business flow. Maya, do you want to give a 30 second on goals?
00:00:27 Maya: Yeah sure, um we want to surface per-feature spend for the product teams and make sure we can attribute cost to model variants. Also Priya is looking for monthly chargeback exports.
00:00:38 Priya: yes, chargeback and anomalies. we had a weird spike last month and no one could say where tokens went.
00:00:45 Daniel: got it. i'll start by opening the "Usage Forensics" dashboard -- it's the per-route view, sometimes the UI says "Usage Forensix" in the transcriber ha ha, but it's the same.
00:01:05 [Screen share starts] Daniel: here is the console landing, top left we've got the time range selector, then below is our per-route table. routes are the API routes you register with Redwood, so each product/service can have its own route id.
00:01:30 Daniel: you can see columns for total tokens, model used, average latency, unit cost, and an "attribution" column which maps to the team tag.
00:01:45 Carlos: quick question — how do you handle shared caches, like when two routes hit the same KV cache or prefix? will costs be double counted?
00:01:57 Daniel: good call. the console does prefix-aware attribution: we surface cached hit percentages and there's a cache-adjusted token counter which attempt to allocate saved tokens back to the originating route. it's not perfect for multi-tenant caches but we add a proportional allocation heuristic. sometimes transcriptions call that K-V cash instead of KV cache, sorry.
00:02:25 Sophie: for Dedicated customers we can do even deeper instrumentation — bind a GPU pool to a project and get per-container metrics, so chargeback is exact at the host level.
00:02:40 Maya: can you show the anomaly detection? that was our big ask.
00:02:48 Daniel: yep navigate to Alerts -> Cost Anomalies. this uses a sliding baseline plus model-aware seasonality. here's a real example — spike flagged for the 3rd of last month, you can see the route, model, percent over baseline, and a suggested root cause (longer sequences on v2-large).
00:03:16 Priya: does that alert include request samples? we need example payloads for audit.
00:03:22 Daniel: yes, each anomaly has a sample set and an optional request export. we also surface the tokens/time series and the top contributing user ids if you're passing user_id.
00:03:40 Tom: security — how do we lock down exports? we can't let anyone pull raw PII.
00:03:46 Daniel: exports respect RBAC and SSO groups. you can also enable field-level redaction on exports and require an audit justification. we integrate with SAML/Snowflake crowd? sometimes transcriber mangles SAML — it's S-S-A-M-L, yes.
00:04:08 Sophie: also KMS integration for key management — customer-managed keys are supported for Private and Dedicated. Carlos, we'll share the KMS integration doc after the call.
00:04:21 Carlos: ok. on the billing side, do you expose per-route unit price? like tokens * rate per model?
00:04:29 Daniel: yes. in the table you can pivot by model and by route. unit price is derived from your pricing profile — for hosted it's public, for Dedicated it's based on committed capacity with amortized infra. you can see both token cost and GPU-hour amortization breakdown.
00:04:50 Maya: show how to split costs across two teams that share a route — tagging?
00:04:57 Daniel: we have route-level tags and request-level metadata. if you send team=nlp in metadata, the console will break down costs by metadata dimensions. otherwise, tag-based allocation rules apply.
00:05:20 [00:05:20] Daniel: switching to the visualization panel: here's per-minute token burn, and below is a stacked breakdown by route, you can click a route to drill to model-level.
00:05:40 [00:05:40] Sophie: quick note: the console retention defaults to 90 days for detailed request-level traces, but enterprise customers can extend this to 13 months with our compliance tier.
00:05:55 Priya: that might be enough, we need 12 months for audits. what's the cost?
00:06:00 Sophie: we'll send options; it's a tiered add-on.
00:06:06 Maya: can we export the exact CSV that we would give to finance? like per-team per-month with columns for model, tokens, unit cost, and latency?
00:06:15 Daniel: yes — export -> chargeback CSV. you can choose aggregation period and dimension. I'll generate one sample now for last month.
00:06:30 [00:06:30] Daniel: exported CSV contains route_id, route_name, team_tag, model, total_tokens, cached_tokens, billable_tokens, unit_cost_usd, infra_amort_usd, total_charge_usd.
00:06:48 Priya: good — can we map infra_amort to our internal DC allocation?
00:06:54 Daniel: we include custom cost mapping keys — you can import your internal G/L codes and map them to routes.
00:07:10 Carlos: question on model variants: we run a canary and a fallback. how is multi-variant traffic billed and shown?
00:07:18 Daniel: the console has model-version attribution per request. if you do a canary split the table will show percentage of traffic by model and the charge will be split accordingly. we also show rollback windows and if fallback to a cheaper variant occurred.
00:07:36 Maya: do you show function calling vs raw text tokens? we use a lot of tool-calls and function outputs are huge sometimes.
00:07:44 Daniel: yes we separate prompt tokens, completion tokens, and tool tokens. there's a "token type" filter. also a little caveat: some tool call payloads may be double-counted if not piped through the same request id, we document that in best practices.
00:08:05 [00:08:05] Sophie: let's demo a detective workflow — find the cause of a token spike and generate the chargeback for the offending team.
00:08:15 [00:08:15] Daniel: filter to the spike window -> group by route -> sort by billable_tokens -> click top route -> view request samples. here's an example request with 14k completion tokens due to long generated transcript.
00:08:35 Priya: 14k? that's the one. we see that. can you show the timeline?
00:08:40 Daniel: timeline shows a sudden increase in sequence length starting at 02:13 UTC, and the top user ids are from an internal integration. there's a distribution chart.
00:08:55 Maya: can we set alerts on median sequence length per route?
00:08:59 Daniel: yes, metric alerts — median seq length, p95 latency, billable tokens. alerting integrates with PagerDuty, Slack, and email.
00:09:18 Tom: on Dedicated, what's the expected p95 latency vs hosted? we need <250ms for our chat endpoint.
00:09:27 Daniel: p95 depends on model and batch settings; for a typical 7b model on Dedicated we see p95 ~120ms for 512 tokens with our batching. i'll attach a model-by-model p95 table.
00:09:43 Sophie: note that latency numbers differ by region and maintenance windows, and our console shows live SLO adherence.
00:09:55 [00:09:55] Daniel: switching to the Optimize tab — this suggests batching and quantization profiles per route. for routes with high throughput, Optimize recommends int8 quantization and a batch size to reduce cost by ~30% with <2% quality regression.
00:10:20 Priya: that 30% is attractive. how do you measure quality regression?
00:10:25 Daniel: we run evals tied to your prompt set and compute regression on key metrics. you can pin a roll-out if the eval score stays within a threshold.
00:10:38 Maya: can we run those evals on our private data?
00:10:41 Sophie: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can run the evals in your VPC or on-prem so data never leaves your network.
00:10:51 Carlos: legal will want to see data flow diagrams for Private installs.
00:10:55 Sophie: we'll share the network diagram and the deployment manifest.
00:11:05 [00:11:05] Daniel: back to the billing view — here's a sample chargeback report exported as CSV. notice you can toggle to show amortized infra vs token-only costs.
00:11:25 Priya: do you support currency conversion for our EMEA teams?
00:11:29 Daniel: yes, monthly rates convert to local currencies and we provide per-region invoices.
00:11:38 Maya: what about cost forecasting? we need to budget for Q1 and want to know how model upgrades affect spend.
00:11:45 Daniel: Forecasting tab — simulate traffic growth, model upgrades, and different batching settings. here's a scenario: move 25% traffic to a larger model — here's projected +42% token cost but infra amortization only +8%.
00:12:05 Tom: is there an API to pull chargeback numbers programmatically? our internal FinOps pipeline needs automation.
00:12:10 Daniel: yes, we provide a chargeback export API endpoint and an S3 export option for nightly dumps.
00:12:20 [00:12:20] Sophie: let's talk about next steps — a short pilot on Dedicated to replicate your spike and validate alerting. Carlos will provide sample traffic and we'll do a 2-week run.
00:12:35 Carlos: sounds good. timeline wise we want this in November if possible.
00:12:40 Sophie: we'll try to spin up a pilot by Nov 24 — Daniel, can you own the benchmark config?
00:12:46 Daniel: yea, i'll prepare the scripts and share them.
00:12:50 Priya: last security question: do you keep request-level payloads for hosted customers?
00:12:56 Sophie: default hosted stores request-level traces for 90 days; Private can retain longer and you can opt-in/out of storing raw payloads. all storage is encrypted at rest with KMS.
00:13:12 Maya: okay that's fine.
00:13:18 [00:13:18] Sophie: we're about halfway through the time but wanted to leave room for questions later — any deep technical dive requests?
00:13:26 Maya: maybe follow-up on model attribution accuracy — sometimes our canary traffic reports show missing variants.
00:13:33 Daniel: that's likely instrumentation — we rely on request metadata for attribution. we'll include a checklist for request ids and model headers.
00:13:46 [00:13:46] Daniel: moving on, quick demo of the per-route detail page: top right there's an "Export for Finance" button that includes attached metadata and an audit trail. clicking it appends who exported and the justification.
00:14:07 Priya: that's perfect for our compliance audits.
00:14:12 [00:14:12] Maya: any caveats with embeddings? we batch embeddings and store vectors externally. how are embedding calls billed and attributed?
00:14:21 Daniel: embedding calls appear like any other route but you can tag them as vector-indexing operations; the console separates embeddings cost and shows index build vs query costs if you integrate with our caching layer.
00:14:40 Carlos: about anomalies — can anomalies be auto-annotated with suspected cause? that would speed triage.
00:14:48 Daniel: yes, we surface a suggested root cause and top contributing dimensions, and you can annotate and save investigations. the transcriber sometimes calls that the "investigatron" but it's just the investigation UI.
00:15:05 Sophie: ok let's pause demo and go into Q&A — we're short on time but want to capture follow-ups.
00:15:12 [00:15:12] Q&A and miscellaneous clarifications (rapid fire)
00:15:18 Priya: will exports include tag descriptions? our internal tags have free-form names.
00:15:23 Daniel: yes you can include tag descriptions and map tags to canonical team ids for clean exports.
00:15:30 Maya: do you support row-level security if we push data to your BI workspace?
00:15:35 Daniel: yes for Private we can set up row-level controls when using our managed warehouse connector.
00:15:44 Carlos: what's typical onboarding time for a Dedicated pilot?
00:15:48 Sophie: usually 2–3 weeks for reservation and infra, 1 week for config; pilot can start within three weeks assuming approvals.
00:16:00 [00:16:00] Sophie: alright we'll wrap up — quick recap of action items then we'll drop links in chat.
00:16:08 Sophie: recap: 1) Daniel to share benchmark config and p95 table, 2) Sophie to send pricing and SOC2/ISO docs, 3) Carlos to share route traffic CSV.
00:16:22 Tom: thanks everyone, looking forward to the pilot.
00:16:27 Sophie: thanks, we'll follow up via email and push the schedule into your calendar.

[Note: the remaining 30 minutes were an extended deep-dive between Daniel and Carlos about benchmark tuning and infra mappings; transcription picks up intermittently with technical snippets and some crosstalk]

00:20:00 Daniel: for the Dedicated benchmark I'll use a synthetic generator that replicates your median seq length and your burst pattern. will test batch sizes of 8,16,32 and measure p95 and tokens/sec.
00:22:15 Carlos: please include the fallback scenarios — our production has 3 model fallbacks and a third-party reranker.
00:25:05 Daniel: noted, will include reranker in the pipeline. also export will include a column reranker_calls and reranker_tokens.
00:29:50 [00:29:50] Daniel: small note, sometimes the console tags the route as "unknown" if the route header is missing; recommended best practice is to always send route_id and request_id.
00:33:12 Carlos: okay attached is the CSV in the chat. also looping our security folks if they have more questions.
00:36:05 Priya: do you have a sample chargeback invoice template we can run by finance?
00:36:20 Sophie: yes i'll attach a template in the follow-up email.
00:40:00 [00:40:00] Sophie: final check — any blockers to moving to pilot?
00:40:08 Carlos: only internal approvals, otherwise no technical blockers.
00:40:15 Maya: agree, we need legal signoff for the Dedicated contract.
00:40:21 Sophie: great. we'll send contracts and the SOC2 pack.
00:40:30 [00:40:30] Meeting end: 46:00 total

Attachments referenced: per-route-pricing-sheet.xlsx (Sophie), SOC2-and-ISO-summary.pdf (Sophie), KMS-integration-guide.pdf (Sophie), sample-benchmark-scripts.tar.gz (Daniel), AtlasBio-route-traffic.csv (Carlos)

Record notes: transcription has a few mis-terms (K-V cash, investigatron) and occasional speaker labeling mismatch.
